response.original_title: La lutte des femmes à Lip et ailleurs
response.overview: In June 1975, in Lyon, 80 participants—hailing from the Lip watch factory in Besançon, as well as other factories, hospitals, the postal and telecommunications service (PTT), and the MLAC (Movement for the Freedom of Abortion and Contraception)—gathered to discuss the role of female workers and employees within companies and trade union struggles, the isolation of housewives, and the need to include them in collective action. *The Women’s Struggle at Lip and Elsewhere* (*La Lutte des femmes à Lip et ailleurs*) is a direct recording of these discussions, conceived as a tool for mobilization.
response.title: La lutte des femmes à Lip et ailleurs
